findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the top-level Acceptance criteria and KERNEL proposal with the final toolset-wrapper mechanism from Phase 2 scope expansion (mark the prompt-only path as superseded and promote the held-out oracle thresholds to the formal AC list).
evidence: KERNEL: 'Co-locate an affirmative per-criterion banking directive INTO the manifest'

Phase 2 scope expansion: 'Three independent prompt-only repairs were rejected by the unchanged live oracle... The residual mechanism is parallel/batched tool execution: instruction text cannot mechanically stop multiple repository tools in one model response.'
The final File impact/mechanism is the agent_call.build_agent_kwargs wrapper, not the manifest directive.
findings.finding: The formal '## Acceptance criteria' checklist and the 'Proposed resolution (KERNEL, affirmative-framed)' describe a prompt-only fix (co-locate banking directive into the manifest), but the later 'Phase 2 scope expansion after held-out RED' explicitly states three prompt-only repairs were REJECTED and the delivered mechanism is now a toolset-wrapper interceptor. The top-of-plan ACs and KERNEL proposal are stale relative to the final mechanism, so an executor reading top-down would implement the abandoned approach.
findings.location: ## Acceptance criteria / ## Proposed resolution (KERNEL) vs ## Phase 2 scope expansion after held-out RED
scenarios: An executor implements the manifest-directive KERNEL fix that the plan already proved insufficient.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace or annotate the '## Acceptance criteria' block so it enumerates the wrapper deliverable's ACs (0/3 RED current prompt, >=2/3 GREEN repaired, simple control PASS, mutation returns RED, wrapper unit tests) and mark the KERNEL prompt-only proposal as superseded.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the new tool-execution wrapper against the three existing WrapperToolset layers in src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py (_steering_toolsets, _memo_toolsets, _runaway_guard_toolsets): state why a new wrapper is needed rather than extending _steering_toolsets, reuse the established asyncio.Lock parallel-batch idiom from _memo_toolsets, and specify the wrapper's position in the steering->memo->runaway composition (build_agent_kwargs, agent_call.py:327-347).
evidence: Plan proposes: 'installs a shared wrapper across its toolsets ... executes at most one read_file/list_directory/search_files call per model response; additional calls in that response receive a steering notice without executing ... An asyncio lock serializes a parallel batch so the bound is deterministic.'

src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py:100 `_steering_toolsets` already 'returns the steering notice past it — keeping tool definitions advertised' via `if ctx.run_step > self.limit: return TOOL_STEP_STEERING_NOTICE`.

src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py:136-142 `_memo_toolsets` already uses a per-signature `asyncio.Lock` so 'a PARALLEL batch of N identical calls in ONE turn ... still executes the wrapped tool exactly once'.
src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py:268-273 `_runaway_guard_toolsets` already keys behavior per model response on `ctx.run_step` with the comment 'a parallel batch shares one step number'.

The plan's expansion text and '## Updated file impact' never reference _steering_toolsets / _memo_toolsets / _runaway_guard_toolsets, nor state where the new wrapper sits in the existing steering->memo->runaway composition assembled at agent_call.py:327-347.
findings.finding: The Phase-2 toolset-wrapper mechanism reinvents primitives that already exist as three WrapperToolset layers in the same module (src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py) without citing that prior art or justifying a fourth wrapper.
findings.location: Plan section '## Phase 2 scope expansion after held-out RED' (the pydantic-ai toolset wrapper seam paragraph); updated file impact does not list agent_call.py additions in relation to existing wrappers
scenarios: Author builds a fourth, near-duplicate WrapperToolset instead of parameterizing/extending `_steering_toolsets` (which already does 'advertise-but-steer-past-a-boundary') and reusing the `_memo_toolsets` parallel-batch lock idiom.

The new wrapper is inserted at the wrong point in the steering->memo->runaway stack (build_agent_kwargs orders them innermost-to-outermost), producing surprising interaction (e.g., memo caching a steered notice, or the runaway guard counting steered calls).
findings.suggested_fix: In the Phase-2-expansion section, add a short prior-art paragraph citing the three existing wrappers; either (a) extend `_steering_toolsets` with a per-cycle one-call-per-response bound (it already advertises-but-steers past a boundary and reads ctx.run_step), reusing `_memo_toolsets`'s per-key asyncio.Lock pattern for the parallel-batch serialization, or (b) if a distinct wrapper is truly warranted, name its exact slot in the innermost->outermost order and describe its interaction with the memo cache and runaway signature window.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the successor_system_prompt reference inventory via find_referencing_symbols and add tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py to the caller-sweep and deterministic run list (or state why its static-prefix assertion is out of scope for the addendum rewrite).

Plan focused-suite command lists only test_completion_banking.py / test_completion_token_recovery.py / test_agent_call_runaway_guard_c827.py — no test_completion_prefetch.py
tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py:321-322: 'successor = cb.successor_system_prompt(None)' + 'assert "prefetched_file_contents" in successor'
findings.finding: The 'Caller and compatibility scope' inventory for successor_system_prompt claims it 'feed[s] only CompletionAgentStep and their tests' and the file-impact / focused-suite lists name only tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_banking.py, but tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py:321-322 also references successor_system_prompt and asserts on its output. findings.suggested_fix: Run find_referencing_symbols on successor_system_prompt, note test_completion_prefetch.py:321 as a referencing site, and either include it in the focused-suite run command or explicitly document that its assertion targets the static prefix (unchanged by the addendum rewrite) and is therefore unaffected.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the record-tool metadata contract: the exact attribute/key name, its value shape (including the evidence-cycle count), which tool names it governs, and where build_agent_kwargs reads it.
evidence: 'The completion record tool carries private, non-schema metadata naming a three-step repository-evidence cycle. agent_call.build_agent_kwargs detects that metadata only for this run and installs a shared wrapper across its toolsets.'
search_files over agent_call.py for 'metadata' returned (no matches) — the detection seam is entirely new and unspecified.
make_record_tool (completion_banking.py:518-546) returns a plain function with no metadata attribute; the plan does not say how metadata is attached or read.
findings.finding: The Phase 2 wrapper is activated by 'private, non-schema metadata naming a three-step repository-evidence cycle' on the completion record tool, but the metadata's shape (key names, value vocabulary, the count '3', which tools it governs) and its attachment point on the tool object are never defined — and agent_call.py has no metadata-detection concept today.
findings.location: Plan §'Phase 2 scope expansion after held-out RED'
scenarios: Implementer must invent the metadata key/shape; a mismatch between how the tool is stamped and how build_agent_kwargs reads it silently leaves the wrapper inert (RED persists) or mis-fires on unrelated runs (breaking the byte-identity guarantee).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the fallback for a post-bound response that still omits record_criterion_verdict (e.g., steering-notice content that names the required record call, and whether/when the wrapper advances the id or leaves it for the finalizer's met=false backfill).
evidence: The wrapper only 'steers repository calls to the record transition' — it does not force a record call ('Intentionally not a forced tool', cf. agent_call.py:332).

No sub-step describes what happens to the current id if the model keeps responding without ever calling record_criterion_verdict after the bound (advance? stall on the id? leave it unbanked and let the zero-progress guard fire?).
findings.finding: The plan does not specify the fallback when, after the three-call evidence bound steers subsequent repository calls to the record transition, the model STILL emits no record_criterion_verdict for the current id.
findings.location: Plan §'Phase 2 scope expansion' ('After three executed evidence responses it ... steers repository calls to the record transition. One successful record_criterion_verdict call is allowed per response and resets the cycle')
scenarios: A model that, post-bound, emits only prose or repeated steered repository calls never advances past the first id; the run can still exhaust with a partial or zero bank.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Mark the KERNEL/Phase-1 'co-locate imperative into manifest' proposal as SUPERSEDED by Phase 2, and state that primary_criteria_manifest's current imperative text (completion_banking.py:184-188) is to be REMOVED so the manifest is data-only.
evidence: KERNEL step 1: 'Co-locate an affirmative per-criterion banking directive INTO the manifest ... e.g.: "For EACH id below ... IMMEDIATELY call record_criterion_verdict ..."'

Phase 2: 'Keep the criterion manifest inside ticket_context as data only: a heading plus exact ids and criterion excerpts, with no imperative text that conflicts with the prompt's untrusted-input boundary.'

The current primary_criteria_manifest (completion_banking.py:184-188) STILL emits the imperative 'When you judge a criterion, immediately call record_criterion_verdict(...)', so the two phases prescribe opposite edits to the same function.
findings.finding: The KERNEL proposal and the Phase 2 repair give an executor contradictory directions for the same manifest artifact: co-locate an imperative per-criterion banking directive INTO the manifest vs. keep the manifest data-only with no imperative text.
findings.location: Plan §'Proposed resolution (KERNEL)' step 1 vs. §'Phase 2 repair plan' ('Keep the criterion manifest inside ticket_context as data only ... with no imperative text')
scenarios: An implementer following the plan top-to-bottom applies the KERNEL imperative, then Phase 2 tells them to strip it — the intended end state is ambiguous.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line note under the KERNEL heading: 'Superseded by Phase 2 — the banking imperative moves to system authority; the manifest becomes data-only (drop completion_banking.py:184-188 imperative lines).'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'banks zero' headline/root-cause with the Phase 2 held-out evidence that the pre-fix arm banks all five criteria (11 bank points, 3/3), and restate the true observable the fix must change so the RED oracle and title agree.
evidence: Title: 'Epic completion verifier banks zero verdicts'
Proven root cause: 'bank upserts = 0' at both budgets
Phase 2 expansion: 'The pre-fix arm made 17 repository calls before banking all five criteria ... still produced [11, 11, 11, 11, 11] bank points in 3/3 trials'
The held-out oracle now uses '0/3 bounded trials' RED, not zero banking
findings.finding: The title and 'Proven root cause' section assert the epic verifier 'banks zero verdicts' across full and 4x budget, but the later 'Phase 2 scope expansion after held-out RED' reports the pre-fix arm banked ALL FIVE criteria (17 calls, then 11 bank points in 3/3 trials). These two narratives contradict each other on the core observable, so the plan's stated intent ('banks zero') is no longer faithfully proven by its own final evidence, and the RED oracle basis shifts from 'zero banks' to a bounded-trial threshold without reconciling the original headline claim.
findings.location: Title + 'Proven root cause' vs 'Phase 2 scope expansion after held-out RED'
scenarios: A reader/implementer sees the headline defect (banks zero) but the final oracle no longer reproduces zero banking, leaving ambiguity about which behavior the fix must actually change and what the true RED signal is.
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle/reframe the defect to the confirmed mechanism (parallel/batched tool calls prevent the per-criterion bounded loop under a bounded request budget, so the run either exhausts budget before finalizing or over-consumes evidence calls) and state the exact RED metric (bounded-trial banking behavior) consistently across the summary, root cause, and Phase 2 sections.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the current-prompt RED threshold (0/3 vs at-most-1/3) into a single predeclared bar consistent with the bounded-wrapper oracle.
evidence: RED oracle: 'the frozen current-prompt arm banks in at most one of three trials'
Scope expansion: 'current prompt is RED at 0/3 bounded trials'
findings.finding: The predeclared RED threshold conflicts between two Phase 2 subsections: the 'RED oracle and behavioral eval' says 'the frozen current-prompt arm banks in at most one of three trials', while 'Phase 2 scope expansion' says 'current prompt is RED at 0/3 bounded trials'. These give an executor two different pass/fail bars for the negative (RED) arm.
findings.location: ## Phase 2 repair plan > RED oracle and behavioral eval vs ## Phase 2 scope expansion after held-out RED
scenarios: A run where the current prompt banks in 1/3 trials — RED under one bar, not-RED under the other.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the RED oracle bar to '0/3 banked before exhaustion' to match the bounded-wrapper scope expansion, and update the earlier 'at most one of three' wording accordingly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the wrapper's behavior when, after evidence-call steering, the model emits neither a repository call nor a record_criterion_verdict call (e.g. return a steering notice that names the exact record call to make, or define how the finite loop guarantees forward progress toward a bank) so banking cannot stall at zero.
evidence: Plan: 'it continues advertising all tool definitions but steers repository calls to the record transition. One successful record_criterion_verdict call is allowed per response'
Root cause: 'The model treats banking as optional and defers to a final structured emit it never reaches'

agent_call.py:332 comment: the analogous steering wrapper is 'Intentionally not a forced tool' — steering only substitutes a notice for repository execution; it cannot compel the model to emit the record call
Removing repository tool execution does not, by itself, produce a record_criterion_verdict call; the model may emit prose or stop
findings.finding: The Phase 2 wrapper mechanism steers repository calls to a notice after three evidence responses but does not force a record_criterion_verdict emit, so a model that 'treats banking as optional' (the proven root cause) may respond with text-only or no tool call and still bank zero — the very failure mode the fix targets.
findings.location: Phase 2 scope expansion after held-out RED — wrapper behavior
scenarios: Post-steering the model emits a text-only response with no tool calls
Model repeats a search after steering, receives the notice, and answers with a summary instead of banking
findings.suggested_fix: Have the post-boundary steering notice explicitly instruct 'call record_criterion_verdict(id=<current>, met=..., evidence=...) now for id <current>' and state in the plan how a text-only/no-tool response is handled so at least one bank is guaranteed before advance.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the per-cycle evidence counter and its per-manifest-id reset live in the wrapper's enclosing closure scope (mirroring _memo_toolsets), and state how the wrapper detects a manifest-id boundary to reset.
evidence: agent_call.py:128-135 (_memo_toolsets): 'pydantic-ai copies a toolset per run step while PREPARING the request, so instance attributes set inside call_tool do not survive to the next turn' — the same hazard applies to the new counter.
Plan pins the asyncio lock ('An asyncio lock serializes a parallel batch') but not the counter's scope or how 'reset for the next manifest id' detects an id boundary.
findings.finding: The Phase 2 wrapper's per-cycle evidence counter and its per-id reset have ambiguous placement: the plan does not pin WHERE the 'at most one call per response / three executed evidence responses / reset per manifest id' state lives, despite pydantic-ai copying toolsets per run step (the documented hazard that already forces _memo_toolsets to keep state in the enclosing scope).
findings.location: Plan §'Phase 2 scope expansion' ('Per cycle, the wrapper executes at most one ... After three executed evidence responses ... resets the cycle for the next manifest id')
scenarios: If the counter is placed on the toolset instance rather than the enclosing closure, it resets every run step and the 3-call bound never fires; if the id-boundary detection is unspecified, the cycle never resets and only the first id is ever banked.

evidence: vague/subjective terms present: reasonable, sufficient
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider promoting the deterministic child-closure shortcut (item 2 / 6ec8 extension) to the PRIMARY resolution for all-children-closed+certified epics, reserving the LLM wrapper for epics with real file_impact_scope, and justify the chosen ordering with a positive rationale.
evidence: Plan: 'First observed closing epic cf3c-1444-863e-49d7 (4 ACs, graph=True, all 4 children closed+certified)'

Plan item 2: 'For an epic whose every DIRECT child is closed AND certified and whose file_impact_scope is none (child-delivered ACs), allow the child-closure evidence to deterministically resolve child-delivered criteria ... extending the existing 6ec8 child-closure shortcut'
The 6ec8 shortcut already exists in the codebase; extending it is a data-layer change that sidesteps the LLM banking loop entirely for the observed incident shape
findings.finding: The plan makes the higher-blast-radius live-eval-dependent LLM wrapper the PRIMARY fix while demoting the deterministic child-closure shortcut to 'optional', even though both observed incidents (cf3c and the 9895 replication) are epics whose every direct child is closed AND certified — a case the deterministic shortcut resolves with no agentic re-verification, smaller blast radius, and no eval fragility.
findings.location: Proposed resolution item 2 (Optional, structural) vs Phase 2 wrapper
scenarios: Any epic-close where all direct children are closed+certified and file_impact_scope is none — the exact reported cf3c/9895 shape
